A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SK-Adapter research. All 26 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–F, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TMS-eval comparisons, architectural ablations, and generation and editing results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds category-specific scores, a ground-truth ReRigging reference and dataset statistics.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the GRPE skeleton encoder, dedicated cross-attention, frozen TRELLIS backbone, zero-initialized residual projections, flow-matching training and skeleton-guided editing procedure. The appendix architecture and codebooks are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use 24k Objaverse-TMS triplets and the same 140-instance TMS-eval set: 54 humanoids, 63 animals and 23 other objects. The new Other-category columns report existing coverage; dataset illustrations do not establish added training or evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: SKDream and adapted SpaceControl remain the evaluated comparison methods in Tables 2–3 and the qualitative comparison. Posemaster is added only to related work. The ground-truth oracle is a metric reference, not an additional generative method.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 adds a ground-truth control by applying Anymate to ground-truth meshes for an oracle ReRigging reference. Existing splits, training budgets, metrics, 12-view rendering and SpaceControl settings remain unchanged; no rerun of the retained comparisons is established.

E4.justification: v2 adds descriptive analysis of skeleton complexity through the joint-count histogram in Figure 3 and a ground-truth sanity check for ReRigging. The architectural ablations in Tables 4–5 and the appendix failure-case analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The new joint-count histogram describes the dataset rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 add Other-category results: SK-Adapter scores 0.2861 ReRigging, 23.43 CLIP, 20.44 PickScore and 2.3765 KD-DINO. It leads ReRigging and KD-DINO there, but trails SKDream's CLIP 24.52 and SpaceControl's PickScore 20.45. Section 4.4 adds the oracle value 0.2073, and Figure 3 adds dataset statistics. All previously reported table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, the rectified-flow formulation in Appendix A, and the distance and relation definitions in Appendix B are unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about native skeleton-controlled generation, the 24k-triplet dataset, structural and generation quality, and local editing. The added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of native 3D guidance, backbone freezing, baseline failures and architectural ablations retain their meaning. Appendix F preserves the same limitations concerning fine details, faces, text alignment and complex finger topology. The new dataset discussion elaborates the existing motivation.

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters, preprocessing descriptions, baseline adaptation details and the project URL are retained. Appendices B–C preserve the codebook settings, TRELLIS-text-large configuration and 151,316,480 trainable-parameter breakdown.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Posemaster as concurrent work using a fixed humanoid skeleton with diverse poses. It also shortens and repositions the AnimatableDreamer discussion, describing 3D rather than 4D objects and removing the explicit assertion that its configuration is completely different.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and wording improvements, condenses the metrics explanation, expands the dataset description and adds equal-advising attribution. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: New Figures 3–4 show the joint-count histogram and dataset samples. Tables 2–3 gain Other-category columns, and Table 3 adds the KD-DINO direction arrow. Existing figures are retained and renumbered, with limited caption, spacing and page-layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The added category breakdown improves transparency by showing where SK-Adapter does not lead, while the ground-truth ReRigging reference and dataset figures make the evaluation and data easier to assess. These are useful reporting improvements, supported by clearer prose and updated related work; the method, retained performance results and limitations remain unchanged.
